I've had a smart lock on my front door for five or six years now, and I've tried quite a few models. For most people, the ULTRALOQ Bolt fingerprint lock is a solid choice, because it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers tons of ways to lock and unlock. Whether you prefer fingerprint recognition or simply entering a PIN, this lock pretty much has it all.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Apple Home support, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ claims the Bolt fingerprint lock is its first smart lock to fully integrate with Apple Home, and that integration is honestly the feature that drew me in the most. I'll admit I still miss Touch ID on the iPhone. You can lock and unlock the door through the Home app or with Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV as a hub, you can include it in automations and scenes like any other Apple Home accessory, and control it remotely.

For me, though, there's still one missing feature: Home Key support. If you could just tap your iPhone or Apple Watch to get in, this lock would be truly perfect. It really comes down to that one omission, though it's not exactly a deal-breaker.

I hope ULTRALOQ adds this in the next model, because with Home Key, this lock could go from "good" to "nearly perfect." It also plays nicely with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT, so no matter which smart home platform you prefer — or if you ever switch down the road — you're covered. It runs on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, so basic remote control through its app works without needing an extra bridge.

More ways to unlock than you'll ever use

The Bolt fingerprint lock is generous when it comes to unlocking methods. The fingerprint ID can store up to 50 fingers along with 50 codes, you can unlock through the app from your phone, have it automatically unlock as you approach the door, or use voice control via Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. Two physical keys come in the box, so you'll never get locked out if the batteries die. For me, a smart lock without physical keys is a complete non-starter.

You can set up to 50 custom codes and issue one-time or time-limited codes to friends, guests, or cleaning staff, for example. If you rent out your place, this feature alone is worth the price of admission.

There's also a "Lockout Mode" that temporarily disables all electronic access methods, including codes and app access. It's handy for anyone going away on a trip who wants an extra layer of security while the house is empty. It's a feature I never expected a smart lock to have, but it's a nice touch to have.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

I've installed more smart locks over the past few years than I can count, so I'm pretty comfortable with the process by now. If you have the right tools on hand, it takes about ten minutes. Assuming you're swapping in a new deadbolt, there's no wiring or drilling required. A Phillips screwdriver is all you need, though you'll need to replace the strike plate on the door frame as well.

Once the lock is scanned into your Apple Home setup and assigned to a room, you can control it through the Home app or include it in automations and scenes to trigger multiple actions at once — like having the lights come on the moment the door unlocks.

Wrapping up the ULTRALOQ Bolt fingerprint lock

All things considered, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt fingerprint lock is a great option. In day-to-day use, fingerprint unlock will quickly become the way you get in most often. Installation is straightforward too. I've been using it on my office door for a while now, since I often have laptops sitting around waiting to be shipped out and I wanted an extra layer of security. I love the feeling of it automatically unlocking as I approach the door, and being able to track who's come and gone. The fingerprint recognition reminds me of the Touch ID I used to have.

You can pick up the ULTRALOQ Bolt fingerprint lock directly from Amazon or ULTRALOQ's website.
